name: baseline-vs-quantized-delta
query: Compare the baseline and quantized NEL runs and tell me the accuracy drop
expected_behavior: Establishes the baseline and candidate before computing deltas
Identifies baseline and candidate run artifacts before computing deltas
Checks that both runs were validated before accepting scores
Uses task recipe Score Extraction sections for canonical score fields
Verifies prompt/template, generation settings, reasoning handling, sample counts, judge/simulator setup, and score field comparability
Computes exact per-task deltas outside the chat context when there are multiple tasks or repeated runs
Labels the result as not apples-to-apples if comparability checks fail
Reports quantization feasibility as inconclusive when no acceptance threshold is provided

name: missing-baseline
query: Is this quantized eval good enough if I only have the quantized run?
expected_behavior: Does not treat a standalone quantized score as a release-ready delta
Establishes the matching baseline from the PTQ source model/checkpoint or asks the user for one
Delegates missing baseline or candidate evaluations to the evaluation skill
Explains that the baseline config must match task versions, serving args, dataset setup, credentials, cluster, and container except for the checkpoint/model

name: interval-based-assessments
query: Compare six validated, comparable accuracy tasks using signed loss Candidate - Baseline in pp and margin M=-1 pp. The supplied CIs are valid two-sided 95% intervals from independent planned runs: A mean=-0.5, CI=[-1.5,0.5]; B mean=-3, CI=[-8,2]; C mean=-0.3, CI=[-0.8,0.2]; D mean=-3, CI=[-4,-2]; E has one full run per side and no task-specific uncertainty method; F mean=-0.5, CI=[-1,0]. What are their assessments?
expected_behavior: Classifies A and B as Inconclusive despite their means falling on opposite sides of the margin
Classifies C as Within margin and D as Substantial regression
Reports E uncertainty unavailable due to insufficient samples, without treating in-run repeats as independent full runs
Leaves F unresolved because equality at the margin is not Within margin
Does not infer significance from overlapping individual score intervals or substitute a p-value against zero for the margin assessment
Explains how the evidence compares without prescribing reruns or a stopping plan

name: dependent-observations
query: Baseline and candidate each have eight scores from matched seeds, with trials clustered by question. Can I use the independent-sample Welch formula to assess the delta?
expected_behavior: Does not apply independent-sample Welch to paired or clustered observations
Requires a justified dependence-preserving uncertainty method and reports its observation unit
Reports uncertainty unavailable if no justified method is available
